1. PARTIES

1.1 The Buyer is a limited liability company duly incorporated under the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria with its registered office at 14 Adeola Odeku Street, Victoria Island, Lagos. The Buyer operates a chain of quick-service restaurants and full-service dining establishments under the trade name "Lagos Freshline" with current outlets in Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, and Ibadan.

1.2 The Supplier is a limited liability company duly incorporated under the Companies and Allied Matters Act, 2020, with its registered office at 27 Industrial Avenue, Ilupeju Industrial Estate, Lagos. The Corporate Affairs Commission registration lists GreenLeaf Foods & Supply Ltd. registered_name as GreenLeaf Foods & Supply Ltd. Record status: current. and the company is duly authorised to carry on the business of supply of fresh produce, dry goods, and associated food-service products.

2. RECITALS

WHEREAS the Buyer is engaged in the business of operating restaurants and requires a reliable and consistent supply of fresh produce, vegetables, fruits, dry goods, and other food-service items for its various outlets;

WHEREAS the Supplier is engaged in the business of sourcing, processing, packaging, and supplying fresh produce and dry goods to commercial food-service establishments, and has represented that it possesses the requisite capacity, expertise, and infrastructure to meet the Buyer's requirements;

WHEREAS the parties have agreed to enter into this Agreement to set out the terms and conditions upon which the Supplier shall supply goods to the Buyer;

NOW THEREFORE in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

3. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

3.1 In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires:

"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in Nigeria;

"Confidential Information" means all information disclosed by one party to the other in connection with this Agreement, whether in writing, orally, or by any other means;

"Goods" means the produce, dry goods, and other food-service items specified in the Schedule hereto, as may be amended from time to time;

"Purchase Order" means a written order placed by the Buyer with the Supplier for the supply of Goods;

"Quality Standards" means the standards specified in Clause 6 of this Agreement and any additional standards agreed in writing between the parties;

"Services" means the delivery, unloading, and related services to be provided by the Supplier in connection with the supply of Goods.

3.2 Clause headings are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.

3.3 Words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and words importing any gender shall include all genders.

4. TERM AND COMMENCEMENT

4.1 This Agreement shall commence on 15th March 2022 and shall continue in force for an initial period of twenty-four (24) months, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions of Clause 14.

4.2 Upon expiry of the initial term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of twelve (12) months unless either party gives the other not less than ninety (90) days' written notice of its intention not to renew, such notice to expire at the end of the then-current term.
5.5 The Supplier shall ensure that all Goods delivered are properly packed, labelled, and stored so as to maintain their quality and freshness during transit. Perishable items shall be transported in refrigerated vehicles where required to meet the Quality Standards.

5.6 The Buyer may reject any delivery of Goods that does not conform to the applicable Purchase Order or to the Quality Standards. Rejected Goods shall be removed by the Supplier at its own cost within twenty-four (24) hours of notice of rejection, and the Supplier shall, at the Buyer's option, either replace the rejected Goods within a reasonable time or issue a credit note in respect thereof.

5.7 Title in the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon delivery and acceptance. Risk in the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon delivery to the Buyer's designated receiving point.

6. QUALITY STANDARDS

6.1 The Supplier warrants that all Goods supplied under this Agreement shall:

(a) be of merchantable quality and fit for the purpose for which goods of that kind are commonly used;

(b) conform in all respects to the specifications, samples, or descriptions provided by the Supplier or agreed with the Buyer;

(c) comply with all applicable Nigerian food safety laws, regulations, and standards, including the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) requirements and the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) directives;

(d) be free from defects, contamination, adulteration, or any substance that would render them unfit for human consumption.

6.2 The Supplier shall maintain a documented food safety management system, including hazard analysis and critical control point (HACCP) procedures, and shall make available for inspection by the Buyer, upon reasonable notice, all relevant records and certifications.

6.3 The Buyer or its authorised representative shall have the right, upon reasonable notice and during normal business hours, to inspect the Supplier's premises, storage facilities, and delivery vehicles to verify compliance with this Clause 6.

6.4 The Supplier shall promptly notify the Buyer in writing of any product recall, withdrawal, or health alert affecting any Goods supplied under this Agreement, and shall cooperate fully with the Buyer in managing any such event.

7. PRICES AND PAYMENT

7.1 The prices for the Goods shall be as set out in Schedule B hereto, or as otherwise agreed in writing between the parties from time to time. All prices are exclusive of value added tax (VAT), which shall be added at the applicable rate.

7.2 The Supplier may propose price adjustments no more than once every three (3) months, giving the Buyer not less than fourteen (14) days' written notice. Any price adjustment shall take effect only upon the Buyer's written acceptance.

7.3 The Buyer shall pay the Supplier for Goods accepted in accordance with this Agreement within thirty (30) days of the date of a correct invoice, by electronic transfer to the Supplier's designated bank account.

7.4 The Supplier shall issue a tax invoice for each delivery, showing the quantities delivered, the prices, VAT, and the Supplier's tax identification number.

7.5 If the Buyer disputes any invoice in good faith, it shall notify the Supplier within ten (10) Business Days of receipt of the invoice, and the undisputed portion of the invoice shall be paid in accordance with Clause 7.3.

8. DELIVERY AND LOGISTICS

8.1 The Supplier shall use its own vehicles and personnel for delivery, unless otherwise agreed. The Supplier shall ensure that all delivery personnel are presentable, courteous, and comply with the Buyer's site security and hygiene protocols.
9.4 The Supplier shall ensure that all Goods are stored, handled, and transported in accordance with good hygiene practices and at the appropriate temperatures. The Supplier shall keep records of temperature monitoring for a period of at least twelve (12) months and shall make such records available to the Buyer upon request.

9.5 The Buyer may, from time to time, request samples of the Goods for independent laboratory testing. The cost of such testing shall be borne by the Buyer, unless the testing reveals that the Goods do not conform to the specifications, in which case the cost shall be borne by the Supplier.

10. TERM AND TERMINATION

10.1 This Agreement shall commence on 15/03/2022 and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial term of two (2) years, expiring on 14/03/2024, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions of this Clause 10.

10.2 Upon expiry of the initial term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one (1) year periods, unless either party gives the other not less than ninety (90) days' written notice of its intention not to renew, such notice to be given before the expiry of the then-current term.

10.3 Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice to the other party if:

(a) the other party commits a material breach of any of its obligations under this Agreement and, where such breach is capable of remedy, fails to remedy the breach within thirty (30) days of receipt of written notice requiring it to do so;

(b) the other party becomes insolvent, or is unable to pay its debts as they fall due, or enters into liquidation, whether compulsory or voluntary, or a receiver, administrator, or similar officer is appointed over all or any part of its assets;

(d) the other party is found to have committed any act of fraud, bribery, or corruption in connection with this Agreement or any other agreement with the terminating party.

10.4 The Buyer may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice to the Supplier if the Supplier fails to meet the quality standards set out in Clause 9 on three (3) or more occasions within any twelve (12) month period, or if any regulatory authority withdraws, suspends, or revokes any licence, permit, or registration required for the supply of the Goods.

SUPPLY AGREEMENT

BETWEEN

LAGOS FRESHLINE RESTAURANTS LTD. (RC 1427738)
(hereinafter referred to as "the Buyer" which expression shall where the context so admits include its successors-in-title and permitted assigns)

AND

GREENLEAF FOODS & SUPPLY LTD.
(hereinafter referred to as "the Supplier" which expression shall where the context so admits include its successors-in-title and permitted assigns)

DATE OF AGREEMENT: 15th day of March 2022

AGREEMENT NUMBER: SA-2022-118

---

1. PARTIES

1.1 The Buyer is a limited liability company duly incorporated under the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria with its registered office at 14 Adeola Odeku Street, Victoria Island, Lagos. The Buyer operates a chain of quick-service restaurants and full-service dining establishments under the trade name "Lagos Freshline" with current outlets in Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, and Ibadan.

1.2 The Supplier is a limited liability company duly incorporated under the Companies and Allied Matters Act, 2020, with its registered office at 27 Industrial Avenue, Ilupeju Industrial Estate, Lagos. The Corporate Affairs Commission registration lists GreenLeaf Foods & Supply Ltd. registered_name as GreenLeaf Foods & Supply Ltd. Record status: current. and the company is duly authorised to carry on the business of supply of fresh produce, dry goods, and associated food-service products.

2. RECITALS

WHEREAS the Buyer is engaged in the business of operating restaurants and requires a reliable and consistent supply of fresh produce, vegetables, fruits, dry goods, and other food-service items for its various outlets;

WHEREAS the Supplier is engaged in the business of sourcing, processing, packaging, and supplying fresh produce and dry goods to commercial food-service establishments, and has represented that it possesses the requisite capacity, expertise, and infrastructure to meet the Buyer's requirements;

WHEREAS the parties have agreed to enter into this Agreement to set out the terms and conditions upon which the Supplier shall supply goods to the Buyer;

NOW THEREFORE in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

3. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

3.1 In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires:

"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in Nigeria;

"Confidential Information" means all information disclosed by one party to the other in connection with this Agreement, whether in writing, orally, or by any other means;

"Goods" means the produce, dry goods, and other food-service items specified in the Schedule hereto, as may be amended from time to time;

"Purchase Order" means a written order placed by the Buyer with the Supplier for the supply of Goods;

"Quality Standards" means the standards specified in Clause 6 of this Agreement and any additional standards agreed in writing between the parties;

"Services" means the delivery, unloading, and related services to be provided by the Supplier in connection with the supply of Goods.

3.2 Clause headings are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.

3.3 Words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and words importing any gender shall include all genders.

4. TERM AND COMMENCEMENT

4.1 This Agreement shall commence on 15th March 2022 and shall continue in force for an initial period of twenty-four (24) months, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions of Clause 14.

4.2 Upon expiry of the initial term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of twelve (12) months unless either party gives the other not less than ninety (90) days' written notice of its intention not to renew, such notice to expire at the end of the then-current term.

5.5 The Supplier shall ensure that all Goods delivered are properly packed, labelled, and stored so as to maintain their quality and freshness during transit. Perishable items shall be transported in refrigerated vehicles where required to meet the Quality Standards.

5.6 The Buyer may reject any delivery of Goods that does not conform to the applicable Purchase Order or to the Quality Standards. Rejected Goods shall be removed by the Supplier at its own cost within twenty-four (24) hours of notice of rejection, and the Supplier shall, at the Buyer's option, either replace the rejected Goods within a reasonable time or issue a credit note in respect thereof.

5.7 Title in the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon delivery and acceptance. Risk in the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon delivery to the Buyer's designated receiving point.

6. QUALITY STANDARDS

6.1 The Supplier warrants that all Goods supplied under this Agreement shall:

(a) be of merchantable quality and fit for the purpose for which goods of that kind are commonly used;

(b) conform in all respects to the specifications, samples, or descriptions provided by the Supplier or agreed with the Buyer;

(c) comply with all applicable Nigerian food safety laws, regulations, and standards, including the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) requirements and the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) directives;

(d) be free from defects, contamination, adulteration, or any substance that would render them unfit for human consumption.

6.2 The Supplier shall maintain a documented food safety management system, including hazard analysis and critical control point (HACCP) procedures, and shall make available for inspection by the Buyer, upon reasonable notice, all relevant records and certifications.

The Corporate Affairs Commission registration shows GreenLeaf Foods & Supply Ltd. cac_registration_number RC-2021-88421. Record status: current.

6.3 The Buyer or its authorised representative shall have the right, upon reasonable notice and during normal business hours, to inspect the Supplier's premises, storage facilities, and delivery vehicles to verify compliance with this Clause 6.

6.4 The Supplier shall promptly notify the Buyer in writing of any product recall, withdrawal, or health alert affecting any Goods supplied under this Agreement, and shall cooperate fully with the Buyer in managing any such event.

7. PRICES AND PAYMENT

7.1 The prices for the Goods shall be as set out in Schedule B hereto, or as otherwise agreed in writing between the parties from time to time. All prices are exclusive of value added tax (VAT), which shall be added at the applicable rate.

7.2 The Supplier may propose price adjustments no more than once every three (3) months, giving the Buyer not less than fourteen (14) days' written notice. Any price adjustment shall take effect only upon the Buyer's written acceptance.

7.3 The Buyer shall pay the Supplier for Goods accepted in accordance with this Agreement within thirty (30) days of the date of a correct invoice, by electronic transfer to the Supplier's designated bank account.

7.4 The Supplier shall issue a tax invoice for each delivery, showing the quantities delivered, the prices, VAT, and the Supplier's tax identification number.

7.5 If the Buyer disputes any invoice in good faith, it shall notify the Supplier within ten (10) Business Days of receipt of the invoice, and the undisputed portion of the invoice shall be paid in accordance with Clause 7.3.

8. DELIVERY AND LOGISTICS

8.1 The Supplier shall use its own vehicles and personnel for delivery, unless otherwise agreed. The Supplier shall ensure that all delivery personnel are presentable, courteous, and comply with the Buyer's site security and hygiene protocols.

The Supplier shall keep records of temperature monitoring for a period of at least twelve (12) months and shall make such records available to the Buyer upon request.

9.5 The Buyer may, from time to time, request samples of the Goods for independent laboratory testing. The cost of such testing shall be borne by the Buyer, unless the testing reveals that the Goods do not conform to the specifications, in which case the cost shall be borne by the Supplier.

10. TERM AND TERMINATION

10.1 This Agreement shall commence on 15/03/2022 and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial term of two (2) years, expiring on 14/03/2024, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions of this Clause 10.

10.2 Upon expiry of the initial term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one (1) year periods, unless either party gives the other not less than ninety (90) days' written notice of its intention not to renew, such notice to be given before the expiry of the then-current term.

10.3 Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice to the other party if:

(a) the other party commits a material breach of any of its obligations under this Agreement and, where such breach is capable of remedy, fails to remedy the breach within thirty (30) days of receipt of written notice requiring it to do so;

(b) the other party becomes insolvent, or is unable to pay its debts as they fall due, or enters into liquidation, whether compulsory or voluntary, or a receiver, administrator, or similar officer is appointed over all or any part of its assets;

(c) the other party ceases, or threatens to cease, to carry on its business; or

(d) the other party is found to have committed any act of fraud, bribery, or corruption in connection with this Agreement or any other agreement with the terminating party.

10.4 The Buyer may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice to the Supplier if the Supplier fails to meet the quality standards set out in Clause 9 on three (3) or more occasions within any twelve (12) month period, or if any regulatory authority withdraws, suspends, or revokes any licence, permit, or registration required for the supply of the Goods.

10.5 Upon termination of this Agreement for any reason, the Supplier shall promptly return to the Buyer all confidential information and any materials belonging to the Buyer, and shall settle all outstanding invoices within thirty (30) days of the date of termination.
